NOTIFY-001.summary: Owner-authorized assignment and direct-mention email supersedes NOTIFY-001's in-app-only channel prohibition.
NOTIFY-001.was: Vector creates an in-app notification, visible within 5 seconds, for assignment of an issue to the operator, a direct mention (ISSUE-013), a comment on an issue they follow, the return of an intake item they deferred, the resolution of the last blocker on an issue assigned to them, and a due reminder (NOTIFY-005). Vector delivers notifications on no other channel; the only mail it sends is the sign-in link `BASE-ACCESS-001` requires.
NOTIFY-001.now: Vector creates an in-app notification, visible within 5 seconds, for assignment of an issue to the operator, a direct mention (ISSUE-013), a comment on an issue they follow, the return of an intake item they deferred, the resolution of the last blocker on an issue assigned to them, and a due reminder (NOTIFY-005). Assignment and direct-mention events may also send the minimal transactional email defined by NOTIFY-006; all other product notification events remain in-app.

NOTIFY-006.summary: Atomic minimal assignment/direct-mention email intent, immediate Base submission, bounded definite-rejection retries and non-replaying uncertainty; recipient preferences, mutes and erasure apply.

REL-006.summary: Expose parent authoring from issue details and root/child browsing filters while retaining workspace boundaries, cycle refusal, version checks and existing child detachment behavior.
REL-006.was: An issue has at most one parent. Vector rejects self-parenting and ancestry cycles; changing a parent never changes status, team, project, cycle, or assignee, and deleting a parent makes each direct child a root issue.
REL-006.now: An issue has at most one parent. An operator can set, replace, or clear it from issue details. Vector rejects self-parenting and ancestry cycles; changing a parent never changes status, team, project, cycle, or assignee, and deleting a parent makes each direct child a root issue. Issue lists can filter to roots or to children of one exact parent (VIEW-001).

SEARCH-001.summary: Global full-text search also indexes saved-view names; searchable issue text, project names and label names remain included, with archived issue/project visibility controlled by the operator.
SEARCH-001.was: Search covers issue identifiers, titles, descriptions, expected outcomes, customer impact, comments, evidence summaries, project names, and label names, and returns within 500ms. Issues of archived teams and projects are excluded unless the operator asks for them.
SEARCH-001.now: Search covers issue identifiers, titles, descriptions, expected outcomes, customer impact, comments, evidence summaries, project names, label names, and saved-view names visible to the operator, and returns within 500ms. Issues of archived teams and projects are excluded unless the operator asks for them.

SEARCH-002.summary: Exact primary identifiers rank first alongside bounded full-text issue/project/accessible-view results; failed index reads retain only a newly admitted primary result. Forward migration 0018 stores stable source TEXT IDs in FTS and joins by ID, preserving identity across source rowid changes and index rebuilds.
SEARCH-002.was: An exact issue identifier lookup reads the primary record and returns it even while full-text indexing is delayed or failed.
SEARCH-002.now: An exact issue identifier lookup reads the primary record and returns it even while full-text indexing is delayed or unavailable, subject to the archive choice in SEARCH-001. On a successful full-text read, that exact issue ranks first, without duplicating it or dropping other matching issues, projects or accessible saved views; results remain bounded. Primary identity, archive choice and operator/session/workspace admission are rechecked before returning results, including after an index failure.

SEARCH-003.summary: Source-transaction triggers retain immediate atomic indexing while migration 0018 replaces rowid mappings with stable source TEXT IDs. FTS read failure retains the admitted exact primary exception under SEARCH-002; other failures remain visibly unavailable.
SEARCH-003.was: Created or changed searchable text appears in full-text results within 10 seconds. A failed indexing job is visible to operators with its last successful index time; Vector never presents known-stale results as complete.
SEARCH-003.now: Created or changed searchable text appears in full-text results within 10 seconds. Database triggers maintain the full-text entries in the same transaction as searchable source changes, so a committed source change cannot leave its corresponding entry behind. If an index query fails, the exact primary-record lookup remains available under SEARCH-002; other searches are reported unavailable with the last successful index time; Vector never presents a known index failure as a complete empty result.

VIEW-001.summary: Parent filters remain; grouped SQL paging orders by group key, selected sort and stable identifier. Page-visible groups retain full-result counts and allGroups preserves the complete aggregate metadata.
VIEW-001.was: Issue lists can filter by status, status category, priority, assignee, team, project, cycle, label, due date, and blocked state; sort by newest, oldest, Urgent-to-No-priority, workflow status order, due date, or last update; and group by none, status, assignee, priority, project, cycle, or team. Completed issues are hidden by default outside Current.
VIEW-001.now: Issue lists can filter by status, status category, priority, assignee, team, project, cycle, label, due date, blocked state, and parent (all issues, root issues, or children of one exact parent identifier); sort by newest, oldest, Urgent-to-No-priority, workflow status order, due date, or last update; and group by none, status, assignee, priority, project, cycle, or team. Completed issues are hidden by default outside Current. Grouped pages order by the group key before the selected sort and stable identifier. Only groups with rows on the page are rendered, with counts for the complete filtered result; a group may continue onto another page. The issue-list HTTP response exposes page-present `groups` with full filtered counts and `allGroups` with the complete filtered grouping aggregate. Positive offsets require the response `revision` for the same query and workspace calendar date; invalidated or missing identity returns HTTP 409 `pagination_invalidated` without mixed rows, and browsing restarts visibly at offset zero.

VIEW-002.summary: Saved queries now include a persisted list or board layout in addition to filters, sort and grouping; the private/shared ownership rules remain unchanged. Successful rename/control receipts update the heading and navigation immediately, invalidate older reads, and still yield to subsequent authorized reads or access denial.
VIEW-002.was: An operator can save a named combination of filters, sort, and grouping as private or shared, then update, duplicate, or delete it. A private view is visible and editable only by its owner; any operator can open or duplicate a shared view, but only its owner can update or delete it, and ownership changes only under OPS-004. Deleting a view never changes an issue.
VIEW-002.now: An operator can save a named combination of filters, sort, grouping, and list or board layout as private or shared, then update, duplicate, or delete it. A private view is visible and editable only by its owner; any operator can open or duplicate a shared view, but only its owner can update or delete it, and ownership changes only under OPS-004. Deleting a view never changes an issue.

VIEW-003.summary: Operator preferences cover the board as well as the issue list; each saved view owns its layout and opening it leaves the source surface preferences alone.
VIEW-003.was: The filters, sort, and grouping an operator last applied to Current, My work, the Projects portfolio, and each issue list are stored for that operator and restored on their next visit from any browser, and one visible control resets them to the defaults. Opening a saved view never changes the stored controls of the list it was opened from.
VIEW-003.now: The filters, sort, and grouping an operator last applied to Current, My work, the Projects portfolio, the issue list, and the board are stored for that operator and restored on their next visit from any browser, and one visible control resets them to the defaults. A saved view's layout belongs to that view. Opening a saved view never changes the stored controls of the list or board it was opened from.

VIEW-005.summary: A team workflow board provides bounded status-grouped paging, complete SQL status totals, keyboard status changes and a phone column selector; it selects the sole team automatically and requires a choice in a multi-team workspace.

BASE-ACCESS-001.summary: Assignment and direct-mention transactional notification mail is permitted in addition to sign-in mail, with explicitly limited issue metadata.
BASE-ACCESS-001.was: Operators sign in by magic link to an allow-listed email address; passkeys may be offered in addition. No passwords are stored.
BASE-ACCESS-001.now: Operators sign in by magic link to an allow-listed email address; passkeys may be offered in addition. No passwords are stored. Separately, assignment and direct-mention notification mail under NOTIFY-006 can carry issue titles, identifiers, readable actors and authenticated app links outside the deployment through the declared transactional-email external.

OWNER-CLAIM-001.summary: Five-minute signed owner confirmation uses Base native bootstrap with trusted deployment configuration, permanent admission ledger and a refused second claim. Local configured-owner setup remains available without RER configuration.

EDITOR-001.summary: The recorded installation owner under current native Base authority receives a non-secret expiring editor configuration grant. The copied same-origin editor is revoked on native sign-out/auth loss and validates the exact management origin; document CSP restricts both framing directions.

API-001.summary: Scoped Base-token routes reuse native issue/list/update/comment/metadata rules without document or file admission.

API-002.summary: Transactional issuance, native publication and safe usage retain current issuer/workspace authority; removal revokes tokens.

WEBHOOK-001.summary: Durable minimal native issue events use Base delivery state, explicit uncertainty and deployment-owned enforcing RPC; no fetch fallback or live delivery claim.

GITHUB-001.summary: Exact raw-byte GitHub HMAC deliveries link explicit identifiers to safe PR URLs/state without a GitHub token or changing issue decisions.

GITHUB-002.summary: Durable replay/current-state/configuration fences prevent duplicate/conflicting/older PR regression and preserve safe portable histories.

DATA-002.summary: CSV/JSON and documented Linear file preflight reports every row error, omitted field, existing native reference and measured bound before publication.
DATA-002.was: Separately from portable restore, an operator can preflight an import of issues supplied as CSV rows or as a JSON array of objects with the same field names, before anything is written. The fields are title, description, team, status, priority, assignee, project, cycle, labels, estimate, due date, expected outcome, customer impact, source ID, and source record ID. The preflight validates the mapping, the timestamps, and every team, status, assignee, project, cycle, label, duplicate, and dependency reference, and reports every row that would fail with its row number and reason.
DATA-002.now: Separately from portable restore, an operator can preflight an import of issues supplied as CSV rows or as a JSON array of objects with the same field names, before anything is written. The fields are title, description, team, status, priority, assignee, project, cycle, labels, estimate, due date, expected outcome, customer impact, source ID, and source record ID. The preflight validates the mapping, the timestamps, and every team, status, assignee, project, cycle, label, duplicate, and dependency reference, and reports every row that would fail with its row number and reason, and every nonempty value it would not import. One preflight covers the whole file of a run, up to the measured run limits in docs/MOVE-IN.md.

DATA-003.summary: A reviewed run publishes in staged batches; each batch publishes all its native effects atomically with current-session and exact native-value fences, and a failed batch writes nothing while earlier batches stay for resume.
DATA-003.was: Applying a successful preflight writes the batch atomically, preserves supplied creation and update times, and records an import-run identifier. A failed apply writes none of the batch.
DATA-003.now: Applying a successful preflight records an import-run identifier and publishes the run in batches, each written atomically, preserving supplied creation and update times. A failed batch writes none of that batch and leaves earlier batches of the run in place for resume (DATA-006).

DATA-005.summary: Public local export/import/export uses one Base engine and exact canonical native records and files. Authenticated restore into a pristine destination bootstrap is locally proven through native Worker HTTP, with atomic session/link retirement, fresh historical-owner sign-in, serialized R2 settlement and unchanged historical-effect quarantine. Hosted HTTPS acceptance remains separate.
DATA-005.was: `pnpm import` restores a portable DATA-001 archive without synthesising activity, audit entries, notifications, or new timestamps; its records are equivalent after export, import, and export as `BASE-DATA-001` requires.
DATA-005.now: `rer import --target local` restores a portable DATA-001 archive without synthesising activity, audit entries, notifications, or new timestamps; its records are equivalent after export, import, and export as `BASE-DATA-001` requires.

DATA-006.summary: One reviewed run of up to the measured limits (tested at 2,000 generated Linear issues) previews once, publishes in staged batches with exact "applied N of M batches" status, resumes after a stopped client or failed batch with each record landing once, and sends no notification, mail or webhook.

DATA-007.summary: After a finished or partial run, Settings and the terminal give one report and one CSV comparing source rows read with Vector issues written by team, status, project, cycle and assignee, every omitted field with its count, every unresolved reference with its row, what the file never held, and each source ID's Vector identifier; old source IDs find their issues by search and lookup.

DATA-008.summary: A Linear API file the owner produces (docs/LINEAR-API-FILE.md) merges with a Linear CSV run: comments with original times and read-only author names, HTTPS links never fetched, and blocks/duplicate relations inside the run; anything outside the run is reported, and a malformed file is refused with row-level reasons and nothing written.

DATA-009.summary: Jira Cloud All Fields CSV uses the reviewed staged importer for a supported profile. Preflight keeps exact bytes and repeated positions, detects dates across all date-bearing cells, requires explicit offsets for offsetless instants, reports every omission and refuses ambiguous or invalid values before writes. Status, priority, active-account, cycle and estimate mappings require explicit review. Evidence remains documented-format, synthetic-only; no real export was supplied.

DATA-010.summary: The Jira supported profile imports in-run parents, correctly directed Blocks dependencies and duplicate-to-canonical links, plus comments with original times and read-only author names. Old Jira keys remain visible/searchable. Exact existing labels, Epic labeling, explicit open-cycle mappings and exact seconds conversion preserve review decisions. Optional named HTTPS attachment links are off by default and never fetched; bytes remain separate. Unsupported columns stay in exact originals and the loss report. No operator, notification or external event is created.

DATA-011.summary: An operator can erase a person that imports carried (exact email and/or display names) after a counts-only preview and typed confirmation: every applied or pending import run, Vector's imported copies, reports and development mail lose them in one D1 batch; issues already written stay, pending runs still finish, and an archive made before the erasure is refused on restore when a later journal is supplied.

HOME-001.summary: The approved public marketing homepage and installed Base Lobby replace the owner identity plate; comparative positioning does not promise feature parity or importer coverage.
HOME-001.was: The public landing shows the configured owner's name, one configured statement of purpose, and a sign-in link. It contains no pricing, feature tour, customer testimonials, or invented metrics. The configured “Powered by <product> · runeditrun.com” credit is shown only when enabled.
HOME-001.now: The owner-approved public marketing homepage at `/` remains exactly as approved, including its copy and assets and the line “100% free, open source alternative to Linear, Jira and Asana.” That line is product positioning; it does not promise feature parity or importer coverage for every named product. The page presents Vector with its headline, one supporting sentence, and source and docs links, followed by short sections (how Current explains each issue, free and open source, deferral, the rest of the product, trying it beside another tracker, a closing call to action), each drawing the product only from its real labels. The public site's “Run Vector” action remains unchanged and points to `/run`, the installation page. The installed application's root `/` serves the Base Lobby, whose Sign in entry satisfies this clause's sign-in requirement (owner decision, 13 Oct 2026 15:11Z). The page contains no pricing, hosting costs, customer testimonials or invented metrics, reads no installation data and is server-rendered.

SETUP-001.summary: Fresh configured installation owners complete a durable same-origin first workspace review; existing configured installations retain completion.

BASE-DATA-001.summary: Portable archive export and restore use the public rer commands instead of pnpm script entry points.
BASE-DATA-001.was: `pnpm export` produces every record and attachment; `pnpm import` restores it into an empty deployment; export, import, export yields an archive with equivalent contents.
BASE-DATA-001.now: `rer export` produces every record and attachment; `rer import` restores it into an empty deployment; export, import, export yields an archive with equivalent contents.

extensionPointChanges.summary: Remove the unsupported import.completed.v1 declaration shipped in the seed metadata. No emitter was shipped for this extension point; staged imports do not emit it.

migrations.buyerSteps: Apply after unchanged 0001–0011, including on fresh installations. Adds a durable cancellation ledger and admission guards; preserves operators, mappings, credentials, outbox and product data without inferring historical cancellation. Back up D1/R2 and validate recovery first. Keep the additive schema and ledger when rolling back application code; never prune or drop the cancellation ledger.

Apply after unchanged 0001–0012. Adds separate administration audit details, durable team issue history and a workspace/prefix reservation ledger, preserving prior product rows, identifiers, counters and closed snapshots. Existing reservations and issue origins backfill the ledger; legacy team history remains conservatively frozen. New reservations survive failed writes and released prefixes keep their consumed numbers. Back up D1/R2 first; validate the populated previous-head transition on a disposable copy. On application rollback retain the additive audit details, team history, prefix ledger and all synchronization and identity triggers; never prune either history or the reservation ledger. The retained team counters mirror the currently selected prefix for compatible prior application SQL. Restore a previous database backup only in isolated recovery validation before any traffic change.

Apply after unchanged 0001–0013. Back up D1/R2 and validate populated previous-head preservation. Adds collaboration, mention sets, exact deferral identity and durable mail state. Backfills only recoverable historical follows, never mail or Inbox history. Keep all additive tables, claims, attempts and accepted/uncertain states on application rollback; never replay ambiguous claims or development captures. Older code remains SQL-compatible but does not produce collaboration events.

Apply after unchanged 0001–0014. Adds the issue_parents relation table (one parent per issue) and its index, with database guards against self-parenting, ancestry cycles and cross-workspace links; existing issue rows are not rewritten and every existing issue remains a root. Back up D1/R2 and validate on an isolated copy. On application-code rollback, retain the table, index and guards; do not reverse the migration.

Apply after unchanged 0001–0015. Backfills full-text indexes for issue text, comments, evidence summaries, project names, labels and saved-view names, then maintains them with source-transaction triggers. A failed index write aborts its source mutation. Validate populated migration and rollback behavior on an isolated copy. On application rollback retain the FTS tables, state row, indexes, views and triggers; do not reverse the migration.

Apply after unchanged 0001–0016. Adds the saved-view layout column, defaulting existing views to list, and indexes for derived issue browsing. Back up D1/R2 and validate populated previous-head preservation on an isolated copy. On application-code rollback retain the additive column and indexes; do not reverse the migration.

Apply after unchanged 0001–0017. Back up D1/R2 and validate populated migration and isolated recovery first. Replaces only derived FTS tables, search document view and synchronization triggers with stable source TEXT IDs; source records and the index-state record are retained. Deploy a stable-ID-compatible search reader with this schema: pre-0018 rowid-based readers are incompatible. Retain applied migration, FTS schema, ID-based triggers, state and all earlier product/identity/mail ledgers on application-code rollback; use only compatible code. Never reverse 0018 or deploy an older rowid reader against it. Validate any prior full D1/R2 backup with its matching source in isolated resources before switching traffic. FTS5 virtual tables may require special provider export handling; test the chosen backup and restoration tool. No application export/restore command is added.

Apply after unchanged 0001–0018. Adds conservative issue-list revisions and independent file-removal custody without rewriting source rows. Back up D1/R2 and validate populated transition. Retain schema and triggers on code rollback; only code that includes detached cleanup discovery, writer settlement and quota accounting is compatible after custody transfers. Never roll back to an older cleanup/quota reader or drop unresolved reservations. See docs/BROWSING-RECOVERY.md.
Apply after 0019. Adds the exact Base development outbox schema.

Apply after 0020. Expires obsolete development-only mail captures and retires their tables; preserves all delivery, auth, removal and migration ledgers. Deploy only outbox-compatible source. Retain new schema on code rollback; validate isolated recovery from backups with matching source.
Apply the shared portability schema forward. Stop local runtime before archive operations; retain provider backups and migration history.

Apply destination access/effect review additively. Restore into empty resources, re-enter secrets, sign in as the archived installation owner and review other access/effects explicitly. Never replay historical pending, accepted or uncertain deliveries.

Apply the Base owner-claim ledger additively after 0023. Preserve existing owners, sessions and every prior table. Existing installations cannot be claimed again. Retain the permanent admission ledger and migrations when rolling compatible source back; never prune it. Re-enter trusted RER configuration and secret setup token only for a fresh signed installation.
Apply the Base D1 import-kit schema after 0024. Preserve all prior data and migration history. Keep originals, provenance, job and reversal journals on compatible-source rollback.

Apply native configuration, encrypted signing values, source/replay/PR/event ledgers and authority/restore guards after 0027. Preserve old records and source versions; retain additive columns and all processed/deletion identities. Restore must exclude credentials/claims and permanently quarantine historical sends. Never reverse the SQL or drop the authority guard.

Apply additively after 0029. It rebuilds oa_sessions to admit the dev session kind, keeping every row, column, index and constraint, adds the dev credential table and recreates the operator-removal trigger unchanged. Retain it during rollback and restore.

Apply additively after unchanged 0001–0030. Preserve prior schema and rows. Retain cycle snapshots, identifier-only membership events, failure entries, indexes and immutable/closed-commit guards on compatible-source rollback. Validate populated upgrade and isolated matching-source D1/R2 recovery before traffic changes. Provider Cron timing remains unproved.

Adds workspace reminder_time default 09:00 and due_reminders delivered ledger plus due_reminder_suppressions per-operator history; expands the notification_type_mutes CHECK while preserving historical preferences. Validate populated prior-main upgrade and isolated matching-source D1/R2 recovery. Use create/copy/swap to expand source record/receipt primary keys with an erased discriminator defaulting to zero, preserving old column values and all unrelated indexes/triggers. Live raw IDs and anonymous erased digests have disjoint uniqueness domains. Retain expanded keys on compatible-source rollback; older code ignoring erased is not compatible. Confirmed deletion hashes external record/revision identifiers. Keep duplicate relations, identifier-only deletion receipts, webhook erasure fences, import erasure hashes, source identities and detached file custody on compatible-source rollback. Use only code respecting erasure fences. Validate populated migration and isolated matching source/D1/R2 recovery before traffic changes.
